_comment: The WebView origin for the Android app is kStorageOrigin in
lib/src/storage_origin.dart. That origin is what partitions localStorage,
which is where the game's saves live.
Changing either value silently gives every existing player a brand new, empty
save -- the old data is still on disk but nothing will ever read it again.
That is unrecoverable for users, so the values below are locked.
An origin is scheme + host + port, so https://localhost, http://localhost and
https://localhost:8443 are three different origins. That rules out the usual
ways of serving a local web app (a local HTTP server, WebViewAssetLoader's
appassets.androidplatform.net) -- they all change the origin and orphan every
save. The app serves the bundled game by intercepting requests instead, which
is how Capacitor's WebViewLocalServer worked too.
scripts/verify_storage_origin.js fails the build if these drift, if the
applicationId in android/app/build.gradle.kts drifts, or if anything calls
WebView.setDataDirectorySuffix (which moves localStorage just as effectively).
Only change them if you are prepared to invalidate existing saves, in which
case set DOL_ALLOW_ORIGIN_CHANGE=1 for that build to acknowledge it.
_lockedReason: initial Capacitor migration; the Flutter app must keep serving the game from exactly that origin or the migration silently wipes every player's saves
